title: Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 25a they said: “What are pigeon-flyers? Here they explain it ‘if your pigeon precedes my pigeon.’ Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya said: Ara.” Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads: “Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya said that Rav said.”

He is likewise mentioned at the end of Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 7, the beginning of chapter 25, and Tanchuma, Shoftim 7: he said, “A person whose eye hurts gives money to a physician,” etc.; in Ketubot 105a the statement is attributed to Rabbi Abbahu. Hyman suggests that possibly he is the son of Rabbi Oshayah Rabbah and was named after his grandfather Rabbi Chama bar Bisa.

notes.text: Ara is the pigeon-luring practice in this passage, not an asserted wooden board or place. Saved Rashi on Sanhedrin 25a explains a trained bird bringing others to its owner, involving theft. The Aramaic term remains in the body, with this contextual explanation.

The consulted Sanhedrin and Rashi support pigeon luring. Hyman’s exact Dikdukei Soferim reading, the other cited passages and the suggested family relationship have not all been independently checked.
